input.body:
Closes #789.

## What

A rule whose whole logic is "these patterns over these files" is now **declared as data** instead of hand-coded. `patternRule(spec)` (new `engine/checks/helpers/pattern-rules.mjs`) compiles a comment-free spec — file scope, relevance gates, and patterns with their failure text — into an ordinary `{ id, severity, description, doc, why, run(ctx) }` rule module, so the runner, `--list`, per-rule overrides, and acceptances all keep working untouched.

## The engine is built for many checks at once

Per the goal of this change, the engine does **one pass over the tree** for the whole rule family, instead of each rule looping every file:

- every registered pattern rule subscribes to the files its scope matches; each file is **read once** and its **lines are split and walked once**, with all subscribing rules' assertions evaluated during that single visit (per line, a rule's first matching assertion wins);
- results are cached per context (`WeakMap`), so the first pattern rule the runner reaches pays for the family and the rest are lookups;
- the `repoHas` gate is evaluated lazily — only when a rule actually produced findings — preserving the original checks' lazy-marker behavior.

Spec vocabulary (documented in the helper's header): `files` (regex or exact path) / `over: 'tracked'` / `exclude`; `gate` (`exists`, `notExists`, `tracked`, `notTracked`, lazy `repoHas`); `line` assertions (`match`, `unlessLine`, file-scoped `when`/`unlessFile`, rule-level `skipLines`); `file` assertions (`if`-list + `require`/`forbid`, per-assertion `gate`); `repo` implications (unless some file matches `require`, flag every file satisfying a `flag` group, anchored at the group's first pattern); `missing` and `maxLines` for exact-path rules. `what`/`fix` interpolate `{match}`, `{lines}`, `{limit}`.

## Converted checks (13)

Each keeps its id, severity, doc, why, and message text verbatim; declarations carry no comments — the pattern plus its `what`/`fix` is the whole check.

- **github-actions**: `gha/label-create-before-add`, `gha/scheduled-failure-escalation`, `gha/unique-automation-branch`, `gha/no-scheduled-fleet-executor`, `gha/pages-artifact-symlinks`
- **chrome-extension-release**: `cer/template-tokens`, `cer/readme-sections`
- **basics**: `claude-md-length`
- **web-speech skill**: `web-speech-recognition-feature-detected`, `web-speech-capture-released-on-pagehide`
- **google-identity skill**: `google-token-audience-pinned`, `google-token-email-verified`
- **unattended-agents skill**: `in-session-github-access`

The workflow-file pattern the five github-actions rules share is now a single exported constant (`WORKFLOW_FILE` in `github-workflows.mjs`), with `workflowFiles()` derived from it.

Not converted (stay as code, by design): parser-dependent checks (`run-pipefail`, `secrets-in-job-if`, `checkout-submodules`, the chrome-extension pair, `leaflet/asset-integrity`), structured-data checks, git/diff/conversation-scoped checks, and `scheduler-workflow-shape`/`task-declaration-shape` (cron math, enum references).

## Behavior notes

Two tiny, deliberate deltas, both tightenings:

- `google-token-email-verified`: the repo-level Google-marker scan now honors the rule's `exclude`, so a marker appearing **only in a test file** no longer arms the gate (it previously excluded only the skill's own fixtures).
- `web-speech-recognition-feature-detected`: the "file already knows the unprefixed name" test is now a plain `\bSpeechRecognition` word-boundary match instead of strip-then-match — equivalent on real code (`\b` never matches inside `webkitSpeechRecognition`).

## Testing

- New `engine-tests/pattern-rules.test.mjs` (12 tests) proves the engine contract: gates, line/file/repo assertions, templating, `over: tracked` vs scanned, exclude, the one-read-per-file pass (asserted by counting reads), and per-context cache freshness. See-it-fail: two engine mutations (dropping `unlessLine`, disabling the `repoHas` filter) each made the suite go red before restoring.
- All **1031** existing tests pass unchanged — including every pack test that pins the 13 converted checks' findings, counts, lines, and messages.

---
name: merge-to-main
description: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
---


The portable recipe for landing the change in front of the owner on `main` — the *mechanics* behind the owner's merge-to-main command (the owner's preferences own the trigger *phrase*; this file owns the *how*). Invoked through the `merge-to-main` skill (this skill); this doc stays the canonical recipe.

**A project's bespoke merge policy overrides this default.** Most projects need nothing here — this default is the whole story. A project that genuinely diverges (a different merge method, a CI/twice-green gate, an extra approval) **states so by naming its merge-policy file explicitly in its own `CLAUDE.md`**. When that declaration is present, read that file first and let it override the divergent points below; when it's absent, follow this default as-is. Don't go hunting for a policy file that the project's `CLAUDE.md` doesn't name.

## Recipe (~4 calls)

1. Load both GitHub tools in **one** `ToolSearch`: `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request`.
2. No PR open for the branch yet? `create_pull_request` (base `main`); end the body with `Closes #<issue>`, and take the PR number from the returned URL.
3. Gate on CI **only if the repo has it** — a workflow that actually runs on PRs/pushes. `workflow_call`-only reusable workflows (this repo hosts some) are *not* CI: they never run here, so a non-empty `.github/workflows/` alone proves nothing; check the PR for check runs instead. No CI → no gate; don't wait for checks that will never come.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Merge directly — don't pre-read status; the call fails loudly if it isn't mergeable.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.

The two divergent points — **`squash`** as the method and **CI gating** — are exactly what a bespoke policy file changes.

## After the merge: capture the conversation (every session, every user)

Once the merge has landed and local `main` is synced, run the growth pack's capture step:
`node .claudinite/shared/packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>` (from the canon repo itself: `node packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`), `<n>` being the issue your `Closes #<issue>` named. Deterministic, seconds-long; it pushes the conversation to the orphan `conversation-logs` branch. It runs **here, in-session, because it needs the live transcript** — the lessons extraction then happens later in the repo's scheduled `conversation-extract` task (MCP-native, with a rethink window), so there is nothing to schedule and no in-session lessons pass ([the pack README](../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/README.md) owns the standard). A later merge in the same session just runs capture again — it captures the delta. In the rare repo that removed the `grow_with_claudinite` pack from `.claudinite-checks.json`, skip this step.

## Don't

- **Don't** re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge; trust it.

While CI runs (merge is armed on green — the notification will wake me to complete it), here's my answer to your question:

**Category 2 — cross-file correspondence — is the natural next append**, and specifically its *tree-derived* subset. Two reasons it fits this exact mechanism rather than needing a new one:

1. **The engine already has the two-phase shape it needs.** Cross-file checks require "collect during the sweep, judge at the end" — and that's precisely how `repo` assertions and the lazy `repoHas` gate already work (per-file visit accumulates state, a post-pass step resolves it). A correspondence assertion is one more state-accumulating kind, not a new architecture.
2. **Its sources often need no file reads at all.** `catalog-completeness` extracts names from *paths* (`^packs/([^/]+)/pack\.mjs$`), `generated-merge-driver` from *filenames* — the pass already iterates those for free.

Concretely, two small vocabulary additions would land four checks:

- `requirePaths: [{ path, what, fix }]` — the degenerate case (file must exist): `cer/release-layout`, `product-wiki-layout`. Nearly free; the gate machinery already covers it.
- `correspond: { fromTree: /re-with-capture/, into: 'sink/file', token: '({name}/', what, fix }` — every captured name must appear (as the token template) in the sink: `catalog-completeness` directly; `generated-merge-driver` with one extra sink mode (a `merge=ours` glob line matching the name) since its sink is glob-semantics, not plain containment.

What I'd *not* force into this engine, despite being Category 2: `version-sync` and `privacy-permission-alignment` extract from **parsed JSON** (manifest discovery, permission-set resolution) — that's the Category 3 axis (selectors over structured data), and bolting a JSON parser onto a text-pattern engine muddies both. And Category 4 (the product-wiki markdown-section grammar) is *thematically* the closest cousin — pure text, line-walking, would slot into the same shared line loop — but its vocabulary (section state, bullet blocks, date grammar, counts/lengths/ordering) is large and all five rules live in one pack that already shares `lib.mjs`; that's better done as a pack-local declarative layer than an engine append.

So: **next increment = `requirePaths` + `fromTree` correspondence**, ~40 lines of engine and 4 checks converted, reusing the pass and post-pass phases as they stand.

> ⏳ **Open items:** CI run on PR #790 is in progress (dispatched manually — app-token PRs don't self-trigger it); on green I'll squash-merge as `LGTM`'d, sync `main`, and run the conversation-capture step. Say the word if you also want the Category-2 append built.

patternRule(spec) (engine/checks/helpers/pattern-rules.mjs) compiles a
data-only spec into an ordinary rule module. All pattern rules share ONE
pass over the tree — each file read once, its lines walked once for every
subscribing rule — with per-context result caching, so a declared rule
costs nothing extra however many exist. Spec vocabulary: file scope
(regex/exact path, tracked or scanned set, exclude), relevance gates
(exists/notExists/tracked/notTracked/lazy repoHas), line assertions
(match/unlessLine/when/unlessFile, first-match-wins, skipLines), file
assertions (if/require/forbid, per-assertion gate), repo implications
(require-somewhere else flag matching files), missing/maxLines.

Converted the 13 pattern-shaped checks to comment-free declarations,
preserving ids, severities, messages, and behavior (all existing pack
tests pass unchanged): gha/label-create-before-add,
gha/scheduled-failure-escalation, gha/unique-automation-branch,
gha/no-scheduled-fleet-executor, gha/pages-artifact-symlinks,
cer/template-tokens, cer/readme-sections, claude-md-length,
web-speech-recognition-feature-detected,
web-speech-capture-released-on-pagehide, google-token-audience-pinned,
google-token-email-verified, in-session-github-access.

One deliberate tightening: google-token-email-verified's repoHas marker
scan now honors the rule's exclude (test files no longer arm the gate).

16	4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Merge directly — don't pre-read status; the call fails loudly if it isn't mergeable.
17	5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.
18	
19	The two divergent points — **`squash`** as the method and **CI gating** — are exactly what a bespoke policy file changes.
20	
21	## After the merge: capture the conversation (every session, every user)
22	
23	Once the merge has landed and local `main` is synced, run the growth pack's capture step:
24	`node .claudinite/shared/packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>` (from the canon repo itself: `node packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`), `<n>` being the issue your `Closes #<issue>` named. Deterministic, seconds-long; it pushes the conversation to the orphan `conversation-logs` branch. It runs **here, in-session, because it needs the live transcript** — the lessons extraction then happens later, in the conversation half of the repo's scheduled `growth-extract` task (MCP-native, with a rethink window), so there is nothing to schedule and no in-session lessons pass ([the pack README](../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/README.md) owns the standard). A later merge in the same session just runs capture again — it captures the delta. In the rare repo that removed the `grow_with_claudinite` pack from `.claudinite-checks.json`, skip this step.
25	
26	## Don't
27	
28	- **Don't** re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge; trust it.

1	# Conformance checks
2	
3	The deterministic-enforcement layer: corpus rules converted into machine-run checks, executed
4	when a session finishes (Stop hook) and in CI. Design and rationale → [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md);
5	which rule came from which instruction → [docs/conversion-inventory.md](../../docs/conversion-inventory.md).
6	Dependency-free Node ≥ 18 — no install step.
7	
8	## Running
9	
10	```sh
11	node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs             # world scope: repo-state rules + settings diagnostics — runs in the test/CI flow
12	node engine/checks/check_the_work.mjs              # work scope: rules judging the current change — runs at the Stop hook (--transcript enables the conversation rules)
13	                                                   # the two are independent runners; each accepts --changed (transitional
14	                                                   # adoption-backlog scoping) and --base REF
15	node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs --list      # machine-readable catalog of every rule, both scopes
16	node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs --init      # write .claudinite-checks.json — the baseline plus the fingerprinted packs
17	
18	node --test engine/test/*.test.mjs packs-tests/*.test.mjs packs-tests/*/*.test.mjs packs-tests/*/skills/*/*.test.mjs skills/*.test.mjs mount/*.test.mjs   # the test suite, as CI runs it
19	```
20	
21	Exit 1 when blocking findings exist; advisory findings never fail a run. In a consuming repo
22	the paths start with `.claudinite/`. The steady state is a repo at zero findings (or reviewed
23	acceptances); `--changed` exists only for adopting a repo with a backlog. **Base-ref note:**
24	delta rules (new suppression markers, commits referencing an issue) and `--changed` scoping
25	diff against the merge-base with `origin/main` (falling back to `origin/master`, `main`,
26	`master`) — and a stale `origin/main` widens that delta, billing the base branch's own
27	commits to the work. So each run **refreshes that ref first** (one `git fetch` of the base
28	branch into its remote-tracking ref — no local branch, index, or working tree is touched).
29	It is best-effort and bounded: no network, no remote, or an unresponsive server and the run
30	continues against the ref as it stands (~10ms to fail, 8s ceiling when a server accepts and
31	stalls; ~0.3s when it succeeds). `CLAUDINITE_CHECKS_NO_FETCH=1` skips it — for a sealed
32	sandbox, or to pin the base deliberately. `squash-merge-history` is one of these delta
33	rules: it scopes to the merge commits the current change introduces since that merge-base,
34	not the repo's whole history, and a merge already on the base branch is filtered out even
35	when a criss-cross or shallow-clone merge-base leaves it inside that range.
36	
37	**Stale-mount note:** a stale mount can likewise surface a spurious finding that an
38	already-merged canon fix would skip — the mount is refreshed by the SessionStart sync hook, so a
39	session that began before the fix landed still runs the older rules. Before committing a
40	workaround for a finding (an `accept` subtree, a suppression pragma), re-run the sync hook and
41	re-check: when the fix is known to have landed upstream, a stale mount is the likelier cause than
42	a real violation.
43	
44	**Vendored/generated files are out of the sweep.** Files git marks `linguist-vendored` or
45	`linguist-generated` in `.gitattributes` — recorded third-party fixtures, machine-written
46	output — are not the project's own code, so the engine drops them from the default file set and
47	**every** check skips them (no per-rule `accept` needed). Mark a subtree vendored/generated
48	rather than accepting each finding it triggers. The one exception is `generated-merge-driver`,
49	which reasons *about* generated files and so still inspects them.
50	
51	## Configuration — `.claudinite-checks.json` (repo root)
52	
53	The declaration is **pack-oriented**: a `packs` entry is a pack id string, or an entry object
54	carrying that pack's own settings — its parameters, and the overrides/exemptions that exist
55	*because* the pack is declared:
56	
57	```json
58	{
59	  "packs": [
60	    "baseline",
61	    { "id": "an-edge-graph-pack",
62	      "config": { "rules": [ { "from": "src", "to": "tests" } ] },
63	      "rules": { "some-rule": "advisory" },
64	      "accept": [ { "rule": "a-rule", "path": "src/shared/", "reason": "..." } ] },
65	    { "id": "a-framework-pack", "via": ["the-class-pack-requiring-it"] }
66	  ],
67	  "rules": { "a-rule": "off" },
68	  "accept": [
69	    { "rule": "a-rule", "path": "src/shared/", "reason": "named cross-cutting concern" }
70	  ],
71	  "maintenance": { "delivery": "auto-merge" }
72	}
73	```
74	
75	- **packs** — the declared packs; the closed set that executes. **No pack runs undeclared** —
76	  the baseline too is declared explicitly (`--init` seeds it; the nightly
77	  baselining backfills a missing declaration). A declared id may name a **canon** pack (mounted from
78	  `.claudinite/packs/`) or one of the repo's **own local packs** (`.claudinite/local_packs/<id>/` —
79	  discovered from the repo's own tree, `local: true`); both are declared and gated identically. A
80	  local pack's canonical declaration token is **namespaced**: `"local_packs/<id>"` (string entry, or
81	  an entry object's `id`) — self-documenting, and a canon id can never be claimed by accident. The
82	  engine resolves both forms to the bare id ([`packEntryId`](../pack_loader/pack-registry.mjs)), so a bare local
83	  id still activates while the fleet migrates (baselining rewrites it; the `local-pack-namespace`
84	  baseline migration tracks convergence). An
85	  **unknown** pack name — one that matches neither a canon nor a local pack — is a settings error,
86	  caught at load (see below); a broken or id-colliding local pack.mjs is likewise surfaced as a
87	  blocking `config` finding, never a silent drop. A pack's fingerprint only *suspects* it is wanted
88	  and never forces or forbids its declaration (a local pack is never fingerprinted or seeded — it is
89	  always declared by hand). An entry object carries:
90	  - **id** — the pack name (required; a bare string entry is shorthand for `{ "id": ... }`).
91	  - **config** — the pack's parameters (e.g. the dirs a technology pack's `npm ci` runs in, an
92	    edge-graph pack's edge list). This is the home of what a legacy top-level `packConfig` key
93	    used to hold — the engine still reads that key, but baselining folds it into the entries
94	    and nothing should keep authoring it. The `pack-entry-config` baseline migration
95	    ([engine/migrations/](../migrations/README.md)) documents the fold; once the fleet is off the
96	    old shape, the key stops being a valid setting.
97	  - **answers** — the pack's adoption-interview answers, **verbatim**, keyed by question id
98	    (`{ "<question-id>": "<answer>" }`). A pack declares its questions on its `pack.mjs`; the
99	    unanswered gap surfaces only as a mild SessionStart note (strict solely inside the bootstrap
100	    adoption flow), never a conformance finding —
101	    [packs/README.md](../../packs/README.md#adoption-interview-questions). A stored answer whose
102	    question the pack no longer declares is an *advisory* `config` finding.
103	  - **rules** / **accept** — severity overrides and acceptances **motivated by declaring this
104	    pack**; they may name *any* rule (declaring pack A can require an exemption to pack B's
105	    check), and the entry is their provenance — the file says which declaration required which
106	    exception. Same shapes as the top-level keys; entry-sourced acceptances surface with the
107	    pack named. Two sources disagreeing on a rule's severity is a settings error, never a
108	    silent last-writer-wins.
109	  - **via** — written by the engine (never by hand) when a dependency is materialized:
110	    the declared packs that directly require this one, kept accurate by the baselining
111	    backfill (an empty recomputed `via` marks an orphan the project can drop).
112	- **rules** — per-rule severity override: `"off"` / `"advisory"` / `"blocking"`. The top-level

attachment.content:
- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- bump-version: Raise the project's version — a minor bump by default. Use when the owner says "bump version".
- generate-project-instructions: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and extract its working instructions into reusable canon packs plus the project's own local packs (.claudinite/local_packs/). Use when a project has no established working style yet, or it exhibits a facet no pack covers — during bootstrap of a fresh/empty repo, or on an uplevel request.
- github-actions-scheduling: What a GitHub Actions `schedule:` trigger actually guarantees — late fires, dropped fires, the 60-day disable — and how to build and describe scheduled work around it. Use when adding, changing, explaining, or debugging anything that runs on a cron in GitHub Actions.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.

pattern-check engine: one pass, checks declared as data

patternRule(spec) (engine/checks/helpers/pattern-rules.mjs) compiles a
data-only spec into an ordinary rule module. All pattern rules share ONE
pass over the tree — each file read once, its lines walked once for every
subscribing rule — with per-context result caching, so a declared rule
costs nothing extra however many exist. Spec vocabulary: file scope
(regex/exact path, tracked or scanned set, exclude), relevance gates
(exists/notExists/tracked/notTracked/lazy repoHas), line assertions
(match/unlessLine/when/unlessFile, first-match-wins, skipLines), file
assertions (if/require/forbid, per-assertion gate), repo implications
(require-somewhere else flag matching files), missing/maxLines.

Converted the 13 pattern-shaped checks to comment-free declarations,
preserving ids, severities, messages, and behavior (all existing pack
tests pass unchanged): gha/label-create-before-add,
gha/scheduled-failure-escalation, gha/unique-automation-branch,
gha/no-scheduled-fleet-executor, gha/pages-artifact-symlinks,
cer/template-tokens, cer/readme-sections, claude-md-length,
web-speech-recognition-feature-detected,
web-speech-capture-released-on-pagehide, google-token-audience-pinned,
google-token-email-verified, in-session-github-access.

One deliberate tightening: google-token-email-verified's repoHas marker
scan now honors the rule's exclude (test files no longer arm the gate).

"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/missingbulb/Claudinite"}}}],"created_at":"2026-08-13T09:46:04Z","updated_at":"2026-08-13T09:46:49Z","run_started_at":"2026-08-13T09:46:04Z","jobs_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31688081482/jobs","logs_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31688081482/logs","check_suite_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/missingbulb/Claudinite/check-suites/85961835277","artifacts_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31688081482/artifacts","cancel_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31688081482/cancel","rerun_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31688081482/rerun","head_commit":{"message":"Declarative pattern-check engine: one pass, checks declared as data

patternRule(spec) (engine/checks/helpers/pattern-rules.mjs) compiles a
data-only spec into an ordinary rule module. All pattern rules share ONE
pass over the tree — each file read once, its lines walked once for every
subscribing rule — with per-context result caching, so a declared rule
costs nothing extra however many exist. Spec vocabulary: file scope
(regex/exact path, tracked or scanned set, exclude), relevance gates
(exists/notExists/tracked/notTracked/lazy repoHas), line assertions
(match/unlessLine/when/unlessFile, first-match-wins, skipLines), file
assertions (if/require/forbid, per-assertion gate), repo implications
(require-somewhere else flag matching files), missing/maxLines.

Converted the 13 pattern-shaped checks to comment-free declarations,
preserving ids, severities, messages, and behavior (all existing pack
tests pass unchanged): gha/label-create-before-add,
gha/scheduled-failure-escalation, gha/unique-automation-branch,
gha/no-scheduled-fleet-executor, gha/pages-artifact-symlinks,
cer/template-tokens, cer/readme-sections, claude-md-length,
web-speech-recognition-feature-detected,
web-speech-capture-released-on-pagehide, google-token-audience-pinned,
google-token-email-verified, in-session-github-access.

One deliberate tightening: google-token-email-verified's repoHas marker
scan now honors the rule's exclude (test files no longer arm the gate).
